key_insight: The paper proposes Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI), a new inverse-problem paradigm that replaces iterative optimization search with methods built from the problem’s mathematical or physical structure.
engineering_relevance: SDI could improve efficiency, interpretability, and parameter decoupling in PDE-constrained inversion and related computational engineering workflows.
method: MSDI: construct a pseudo-inverse in the spectral domain using unitary diagonalization.
PSDI: recover solutions by exploiting physical structure via virtual-source projection or back-propagation analogies.
Position SDI as a complement and extension to conventional optimization-driven inversion.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and programmatic; it does not report numerical experiments, benchmark data, or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: The framework appears broad but the abstract only names representative methods, so practical performance and generality will depend on how well the required structural assumptions hold in a given problem.
paper_title: Structure-Driven Inversion: A New Paradigm for Solving Inverse Problems
